blocks.tamil_translation: at the time of the Battle of Hunain) asked, “Who will stand guard for us tonight?” Hazrat Anas ibn Abi Marthad Ghanawi (RA) said, “O Rasulullah, I (will stand guard).” Rasulullah ﷺ said, “Mount your ride!” He mounted his horse and came into the presence of Rasulullah ﷺ. Rasulullah ﷺ said to him, “Go towards that mountain pass ahead of you. Go up to that high part and (stand guard there! You must keep watch very carefully.) We must not be deceived by a plot of the enemy because of your negligence,” and so he warned him. (Hazrat Sahl (RA) says,) “The next day, when morning came, the Prophet ﷺ went to the place where he prayed and prayed two rak'ahs (the Sunnah of Fajr) there. Then the Prophet ﷺ asked, “Have you received any news about your horseman?” The Sahabah (RA) replied, “O Rasulullah! We have not received any news!” Then the iqamah was called for the (Fajr) Salah. During the Salah, the attention of Rasulullah ﷺ remained towards that mountain pass. After the Prophet ﷺ finished the Salah and gave salam, he said, “Good news for you! Your horseman has come.” When we looked between the trees in that pass, Hazrat Anas ibn Abi Marthad (RA) was coming. He came to Rasulullah ﷺ, gave salam, and said, “I set out (from here) and reached on foot the high part of the pass that the Prophet ﷺ had commanded me to go to. (I stood guard there the whole night.) When it was Subh, I climbed up and looked over both passes, and I did not see anyone.” The Prophet ﷺ asked, “Did you get down from your mount during the night?” “No!”
